# Research

My research interests center on computational statistics and scientific computing, particularly where machine learning and mathematical modeling can reveal structure in complex data.

::: {.research-highlight}
## Directed brain networks with reservoir computing

**Directed Networks and Resting-State Effective Brain Connectivity with State-Space Reconstruction Using Reservoir Computing Causality**  
Joan Falcó-Roget, Adrian Onicas, **Felix Akwasi-Sarpong**, Alessandro Crimi (2023).

This work studies effective connectivity in resting-state brain networks using reservoir-computing causality and state-space reconstruction. It connects time-series modeling, nonlinear dynamics, machine learning, and computational neuroscience.

[Open DOI](https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.06.08.544175){.btn-secondary}
:::

## Research directions

### Statistical machine learning
I am interested in methods that balance prediction, interpretability, and computational efficiency, including regularization and high-dimensional models.

### Scientific computing & optimization
My computational work includes numerical optimization, iterative algorithms, simulation, and matrix-based methods for scientific problems.

### Biostatistics & health data
I have worked with longitudinal and survival-analysis methods and am interested in rigorous statistical approaches to biomedical and population-health questions.

### Reproducible research
I use R, Python, Quarto, LaTeX, and Git to create workflows in which the analysis, figures, code, and final report can be reproduced from a transparent source.
